result.summary: The image shows a signalized urban intersection with marked zebra crosswalks and well-maintained sidewalks. Pedestrian signals and street lighting are present, providing a basic level of safety infrastructure in a high-density residential area.

hazards.name: Wide curb radius
hazards.description: The corner geometry on the right appears wide, which can encourage vehicles to make turns at higher speeds.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the intersection corner

hazards.name: Lack of physical protection
hazards.description: There are no bollards or physical barriers at the corners to protect pedestrians from vehicles that might oversteer.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to reduce the crossing distance for pedestrians and force drivers to slow down when turning.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Adjust signal timing to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles receive a green light, increasing visibility.

result.summary: The image shows an urban intersection equipped with high-visibility zebra crosswalks, traffic signals, and wide sidewalks. The environment is generally pedestrian-friendly, though it features embedded trolley tracks and parked vehicles that may impact visibility and footing.

hazards.name: Trolley Tracks
hazards.description: Embedded metal tracks in the roadway can cause tripping for pedestrians or catch bicycle tires, especially when crossing at an angle.
hazards.location_in_image: Running down the center of the roadway and through the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles on the right side of the street near the intersection can block sight lines between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street, parked along the curb near the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the crosswalk to improve visibility for all road users.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and increase pedestrian visibility.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment includes wide sidewalks, curb ramps with tactile paving, and pedestrian signals, but lacks marked crosswalks and lane markings on the roadway. A pedestrian is visible crossing an unmarked section of the street, indicating a need for clearer infrastructure.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crosswalk
hazards.description: The absence of painted crosswalk markings at a signalized crossing point reduces driver awareness of pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground roadway where the pedestrian is walking.

hazards.name: Lack of Lane Markings
hazards.description: The absence of lane lines on the roadway can lead to unpredictable vehicle positioning.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style crosswalk markings to clearly define the pedestrian path.

interventions.title: Lane Striping
interventions.description: Add clear lane markings to the roadway to organize traffic flow and improve predictability.

result.summary: The image shows an urban street with a marked zebra crosswalk and trolley tracks embedded in the roadway. While sidewalks and traffic signals are present, the presence of tracks and parked vehicles near the crossing introduces specific hazards for pedestrians and micromobility users.

hazards.name: Trolley Tracks
hazards.description: Metal tracks in the roadway can cause tripping for pedestrians or catch the wheels of bicycles and scooters.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway, running parallel to traffic flow.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles on the right side of the street may block sight lines between drivers and pedestrians entering the crosswalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway, adjacent to the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Lack of Micromobility Separation
hazards.description: Scooters and bicycles are forced to share the lane with motor vehicles and tracks, increasing conflict risk.
hazards.location_in_image: Center left of the roadway where a scooter and bike are visible.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve visibility for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and further improve sight lines.

interventions.title: Dedicated Bike Lane
interventions.description: Provide a separated lane for bicycles and scooters to move them away from trolley tracks and vehicle traffic.
